captions.instagram:
How does naturopathy work?

Hip baths, mud packs, fasting and sunshine: naturopathy heals without medicines, and Gandhi was its biggest fan. Walk its 200-year story from a Silesian water cure to Urulikanchan, see its five-element model as it tells it, then watch what hot water, cold water and a 3-day fast really do inside you, and where the evidence stands.

→ Naturopathy began as the "water cure" of 19th-century Europe: cold baths, fresh air and plain food.
→ In India, Gandhi championed it and opened a nature cure ashram for villagers at Urulikanchan in 1946.
→ Naturopathy pairs five elements with five therapies: fasting, fresh air, sun, water, and mud with diet.
→ In a cold hip bath, skin vessels clamp shut and keep warm blood deep inside.
→ In hot water they open wide: 1.6 times wider carries about 7 times the blood.

youtubeLong.description:
Hip baths, mud packs, fasting and sunshine: naturopathy heals without medicines, and Gandhi was its biggest fan. Walk its 200-year story from a Silesian water cure to Urulikanchan, see its five-element model as it tells it, then watch what hot water, cold water and a 3-day fast really do inside you, and where the evidence stands.

▶ Play with the interactive version: https://glassbox-production-fd52.up.railway.app/e/naturopathyclear/

In this video:
• From water cure to village ashram. Nature cure began with Priessnitz's cold-water spa (1822), Kneipp's My Water Cure (1886) and Kuhne's 'one disease, one cure' (1891).
• Five elements, as naturopathy tells it. Naturopathy pairs the five elements with therapies: space with fasting, air with air baths and pranayama, fire with sun baths, water with hydrotherapy, earth with mud and diet.
• What water really does. Cold water narrows skin blood vessels and hot water opens them wide.
• Where it meets good science. Healthy-living parts hold up.
• Fair tests, fasting and detox. In a fast the liver's sugar store runs low within a day, then new glucose and ketones keep a healthy adult steady.
• Using it wisely. Keep the good habits: sleep, daily movement, vegetables, less salt and sugar, fresh air and calm.
